- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- After a recent price spike (e.g., +5%+ from 10-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10% above recent high for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative, model underestimates downward moves; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for 10–15 day horizon.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If sentiment history shows no recent positive signal, model tends to underestimate true price drop; adjust downward by 1–3% for 15–30 day horizon.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early 30-day window (days 1–7); apply smoothing or lag correction for first 5 days.
